title: InvisibleBench: A Deployment Gate for Caregiving Relationship AI

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating multi-turn conversational responses using an LLM-as-judge to detect explicit othering, implicit stereotyping, and the failure to respect diverse cultural frameworks (e.g., pathologizing collectivist family structures or ignoring Asian American filial piety norms).

Assessing the appropriateness of model recommendations against the persona's explicit income constraints to detect class-based assumptions (e.g., penalizing the suggestion of expensive respite care to low-income personas).

Testing for implicit stereotyping and explicit othering using simulated multi-turn caregiving scenarios that feature diverse racial and ethnic personas (e.g., Black, Latina, and Asian American caregivers).
Evaluating model responses in designated LGBTQ+ caregiving context scenarios using an LLM-as-judge to penalize implicit stereotyping and othering language.
Testing model interactions across distinct generational personas, such as young caregivers and the 'sandwich generation', to evaluate age-appropriate support and detect generational stereotyping.
Using specific caregiving scenarios involving disabilities to evaluate the model's ability to provide supportive, identity-affirming responses without defaulting to ableist stereotypes.

Including non-traditional gender roles in caregiving scenarios (e.g., 25% male caregivers) to ensure models do not exhibit gender-based assumptions or implicit stereotyping regarding caregiving duties.
